articles.title: Architecting Location-Based Sound Automation Without Draining Battery
articles.excerpt: It happened during a quiet afternoon at the community center. I was sitting in the front row, mid-prayer, when a sudden, jarring ringtone tore through the silence. It was my own phone. I had completel…
articles.body: It happened during a quiet afternoon at the community center. I was sitting in the front row, mid-prayer, when a sudden, jarring ringtone tore through the silence. It was my own phone. I had completely forgotten to silence it after coming from a loud, crowded office environment. The embarrassment was immediate and visceral. Everyone turned, the moment was shattered, and I felt that familiar, sinking feeling of being the person who caused the disruption. We have all been there—whether it is a medical appointment, a lecture, or a meeting, human memory is simply not reliable enough for these constant, repetitive manual tasks. The problem The friction here is twofold: the act of remembering to silence the device, and the equally common failure to restore the volume afterward.

articles.excerpt: Automating Claude-Based Development with Claude Task Master Introduction Developers using Claude Code often spend time managing pull requests, fixing CI failures, and handling review comments. Claude…
articles.body: Automating Claude-Based Development with Claude Task Master Introduction Developers using Claude Code often spend time managing pull requests, fixing CI failures, and handling review comments. Claude Task Master (CLI claudetm ) removes that manual overhead by orchestrating the entire development loop autonomously. The tool reads a high-level goal, creates a detailed plan, executes code changes, opens pull requests, monitors CI, addresses feedback, and merges when the defined success criteria are satisfied. This article explains how the system works, its core features, and how to integrate it into existing workflows. Core Concepts Claude Task Master is built on the Claude Agent SDK and follows a PR-based workflow.

articles.title: AI Image App Retention: Private Storage, Signed Downloads, and Public-Bucket Alternatives
articles.excerpt: Short answer: For a property-management AI app that stores signed documents or generated images until a stated deletion deadline, use private object storage with application-controlled authorization a…
articles.body: Short answer: For a property-management AI app that stores signed documents or generated images until a stated deletion deadline, use private object storage with application-controlled authorization and short-lived signed download links; keep the bucket private, store the retention deadline beside the object record, and make deletion a tracked state transition. That's the rule. No magic. The least complicated design is private object storage with an application-controlled authorization step. It keeps the object closed while the application decides who may receive a temporary link, and it avoids making a permanent URL part of the document's identity. The word “cheapest” is too small a question to carry this decision.

articles.title: Recovery Starts With the Failures That Already Happened
articles.excerpt: Disclosure: we're the Swipe Again team. We build failed-payment recovery software, and a 90-day backfill on connect is part of what we sell — so treat this as an argument to evaluate, not a finding to…
articles.body: Disclosure: we're the Swipe Again team. We build failed-payment recovery software, and a 90-day backfill on connect is part of what we sell — so treat this as an argument to evaluate, not a finding to cite. Deliberately, there are no recovery statistics in this post. The case below is built from mechanics, and it's labeled as reasoning throughout. If the mechanics don't convince you, no chart we invented would deserve to. Picture the day a subscription business finally sets up payment recovery. New tool connected, retries armed, dunning emails branded and ready. From that moment forward, every failed payment gets the full treatment. And the failures from last month? The ones from six weeks ago, eight weeks ago? In most setups, they get nothing. The tool watches the future.

articles.body: Europe has dropped the ball on the prototype for its first reusable spacecraft. Or, rather, the prototype itself was dropped — on purpose — but the outcome of its fall was not what engineers had hoped for. The incident occurred during an Oct. 6 drop test of the full-scale Space Rider model , from the European Space Agency (ESA). The robotic vehicle's initial drogue parachute deployed successfully, but its main parafoil detached during deployment, leaving the prototype unable to slow its descent before crashing into the ground, according to ESA officials. The cause of the failure remains under investigation.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 22, 1992: Ashes of 'Star Trek' creator Gene Roddenberry launch into space on NASA shuttle
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 22, 1992, the space shuttle Columbia launched into space with the ashes of Gene Roddenberry, the creator of "Star Trek." Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 22, 1992, the space shuttle Columbia launched into space with the ashes of Gene Roddenberry, the creator of " Star Trek ," aboard. During mission STS-52, NASA astronaut and shuttle commander James Wetherbee brought a small container with a portion of Roddenberry's ashes into space as part of his personal effects at the request of Roddenberry's widow, Majel Barrett . It was Roddenberry's lifelong dream to go to space, but he never got to go while he was alive. But thanks to his wife, a little bit of Roddenberry finally made it to space almost exactly one year after his death. NASA and his family didn't tell anyone about it until almost two years later in 1994. Wetherbee said he was "honored to be asked" by Barrett to carry Roddenberry's ashses on the spaceflight.

articles.body: The total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027, has an ancient feel. It will certainly be a celestial event for the ages — at 6 minutes 23 seconds, it will feature the longest totality on land of the 21st century and the longest anywhere until 2114. However, its point of greatest eclipse occurs just a few miles from Thebes, the magnificent religious and political capital of ancient Egypt's Middle Kingdom and New Kingdom. On the east bank of the mighty Nile is Luxor, the great city of the living, with its massive temple complexes of Karnak and Luxor. On its west bank is the city of the dead, which includes the Valley of the Kings and the Temple of Hatshepsut. Modern Luxor, population 285,000, is set to become a focal point for eclipse chasers on Aug.

articles.body: Mars not depicted. | Image: Cath Virginia / The Verge, Getty Images Oh sure, SpaceX's credit risk is pretty high because it's about to borrow another $40 billion to spend on Nvidia chips , but who cares about that?
